text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client with massive hemorrhage. The primary healthcare provider (PHCP) prescribes 1 unit of whole blood to be administered immediately. Which of the following can the nurse safety administer to this client?
notes: Correct: “O negative” – This type of blood is the universal donor.
• “A negative” – May cause an adverse reaction.
• “B negative” – May cause an adverse reaction.
• “AB negative” – May cause an adverse reaction.

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client receiving packed red blood cells(PRBCs). Which of the following manifestations should alert the nurse to a hemolytic transfusion reaction? Select all that apply.
Correct answers: A. Headache.; B. Tachycardia.; D. Apprehension.; F. Sense of impending doom.
notes: • “Distended neck veins” – This is circulatory overload reaction.

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed a blood transfusion. The client asks if any disease can be transmitted from the donor. Which of the following diseases can be transmitted from a donor? Select all that apply.
Correct answers: A. Epstein-Barr.; B. HIV.; C. CMV.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed 2 units of packed red blood cells. W
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed 2 units of packed red blood cells. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement when caring for the client. Select all that apply.
A. Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same.
B. Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours.
C. Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open.
D. Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing.
E. Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots.
F. Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion.
Correct answers: B. Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours.; C. Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open.; E. Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots.
notes: • “Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours” – A unit should infuse in 4 hours or less.
• “Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open” – If a reaction occurs you should stop the infusion and KVO.
• “Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots” – Blood should be inspected for these prior to administration.
• “Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same” – You need to verify units with the client's identifier information not the bags.

• “Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing” – Vitals should be taken prior to administration, every 15 minutes for the first hour, then every hour until complete. Not every 15 minutes for the entire transfusion.
• “Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion” – A 19 gauge or larger catheter should be used so RBCs are not destroyed by the lumen.
